title: To amend the International Religious Freedom Act of 1998 to include the desecration of cemeteries among the many forms of violations of the right to religious freedom.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on May 28, 2014. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Amends the International Religious Freedom Act of 1998 to include the desecration of cemeteries among the forms of violations of the right to religious freedom in many countries around the world.

summary.headline: A 2014 law adds the desecration of cemeteries to the list of religious freedom violations covered by the International Religious Freedom Act.
summary.what_it_does: The law amends the International Religious Freedom Act of 1998, which tracks violations of religious freedom in countries around the world. It adds the desecration of cemeteries to the forms of violations that the Act covers. The official summary does not describe any new penalties, funding, or enforcement steps.

who_it_affects.group: Religious communities abroad whose cemeteries or burial sites may be damaged or destroyed
who_it_affects.how: Damage to their cemeteries is now recognized under the Act as a form of religious freedom violation.

who_it_affects.group: State Department staff who prepare the annual international religious freedom reports
who_it_affects.how: They must consider cemetery desecration when documenting religious freedom violations in other countries.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when the President signed it on August 8, 2014.
